newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra says it Mexicans' top long-distance choice.
newsitem.headline: Alestra says it Mexicans' top long-distance choice.

text.p: New Mexican telephone company Alestra on Tuesday claimed it was the people's top choice in the selection of long-distance telephone carriers.
Alestra, a joint venture of AT&T, Mexican industrial group Alfa and Mexican bank Bancomer, said 41.5 percent of Mexican customers had chosen it as their primary long-distance carrier.
The next closest competitor had less than 30 percent, Alestra said without naming the company.

It said it received its information from the government's official database where the results of the balloting are being tabulated. However, the government has yet to announce those results and has warned the companies against making premature or fradulent claims.
Mexican telephone customers can now choose their primary long-distance carrier since Telmex lost its monopoly status on January 1.
